items.summaryZh: F1积分榜领跑者安东内利在巴库Q1因非受迫失误撞墙，悬挂受损被迫停车，正赛将从第16位发车。他称这是一次“不必要的”失误，并表示自己需要“做得更好”。

media.altZh: 安东内利为巴库Q1撞墙自责：我需要做得更好

items.originalTitle: Kimi Antonelli angry at himself for Baku crash: "I need to do a much better job"
items.summaryEn: F1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashed into the wall in Q1 in Baku due to an unforced error, sustaining suspension damage that forced him to stop and leaving him 16th on the grid. He called it an "unnecessary" mistake and said he needs to "do a much better job".
detailZh: 安东内利为巴库撞车自责：“我需要做得更好”
安东内利对F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛Q1排位赛中代价高昂的撞车感到沮丧，并解释了为何正赛的翻盘会比在蒙扎困难得多。
F1积分榜领跑者安东内利表示，在巴库发生一次“不必要的”排位赛事故、导致他从第16位发车后，他需要“做得更好”。
安东内利在Q1出现非受迫失误，他在开始第二个飞驰圈时，在第一弯左侧弯撞上了内侧护墙，造成悬挂损坏，被迫停下他的梅赛德斯W17赛车。
安东内利的首个飞驰圈本已让他晋级Q2，但由于这位意大利车手无法参赛，他将在周六从第16位发车，面临一场翻盘之战。更糟的是，梅赛德斯在巴库证明了自己是全场标杆，队友乔治·拉塞尔以0.8秒的优势碾压对手夺得杆位，这意味着安东内利很可能白白错失了一个头排发车位。
“那只是对抓地力变化如此之大的一个误判，”安东内利解释道。“在Q1这是一次不必要的失误，这也是一个很好的提醒：像这样，事情不会顺我的意，所以我需要做得更好。”
“与上一圈相比，我遇到了更大的逆风，所以前轮抓地力强了很多，我在大致相同的位置入弯，但显然赛车转向更多，我蹭到了墙。”
由于液压问题，安东内利错过了周四的大部分练习，这位20岁的车手整个周末本就处于被动，因此他承认自己“没有百分之百在状态”，而拉塞尔本就会很难被击败。
“乔治这个周末做得非常出色，”安东内利承认。“他对赛车的感觉非常好，所以肯定是他拉开了差距。我必须对此诚实，但赛车也确实非常非常快。”
上一次安东内利从队尾发车时，这位意大利人在主场蒙扎上演了一场堪称经典的驾驶，完成了一次壮观的翻盘胜利。
但尽管巴库6公里的街道赛道在其长直道上也提供了超车机会，安东内利警告说，要复制蒙扎的翻盘会困难得多。
“好的起步，远离麻烦，然后努力跑出非常好的节奏，”安东内利这样总结他周六的计划。“显然，这会比蒙扎更难一些，因为这里超车更难，但我相信我们仍然能跑出一场好比赛。”
“我没有什么可失去的，我只需要尽我所能跑出最好的比赛。随着经验积累，你会学会如何向前推进。当然，这个周末一切都有点不顺，但明天我认为我们能跑出一场好比赛。”
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli angry at himself for Baku crash: "I need to do a much better job"
Kimi Antonelli was left frustrated by a costly Q1 qualifying crash at Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, and explained why a comeback race will be much harder than in Monza
F1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he needs to "do a much better job" after an "unnecessary" qualifying incident in Baku left him 16th on the grid.

Antonelli made an unforced error in Q1 when he tagged the inside wall in Turn 1 left-hander to start his second flying lap, sustaining terminal suspension damage that forced him to park his Mercedes W17.

Antonelli's first lap had already qualified him for Q2, but with the Italian unable to take part, he is facing a comeback race on Saturday from 16th on the grid. To add insult to injury, Mercedes proved the class of the field in Baku as team-mate George Russell demolished the competition to take pole by eight tenths, meaning Antonelli likely cost himself a front-row start.

"It was just a misjudgement with the grip changing so much," Antonelli explained. "An unnecessary one in Q1, and it's a very good reminder that like this,  things don't go my way, so I need to do a much better job.
"I had a lot more headwind compared to the lap before, so the front just was much stronger, and I turned in roughly in the same spot, but obviously the car turned more and I clipped the wall."

With Antonelli missing a large chunk of Thursday practice due to a hydraulic issue, the 20-year-old had already been on the back foot all weekend, so he acknowledged he "wasn't 100 percent there" and Russell would have been tough to beat.

"George has been doing an incredible job this weekend," Antonelli admitted. "He's been feeling very good with the car, so for sure he has made the difference. I have to be honest with that, but also the car has been very, very quick."
The last time Antonelli started from the rear of the grid, the Italian put in a drive for the ages with a spectacular comeback win on home soil in Monza.
But while Baku's 6km street circuit also offers overtaking potential on its long straight, Antonelli cautioned a Monza repeat would be much more difficult to pull off.

"A good start, stay out of trouble, and then try to set a really good pace," Antonelli summed up his Saturday plans. "Obviously, it's going to be a bit harder than Monza because it's a bit harder to overtake here, but I believe we can still do a good race.

"I have nothing to lose, and I just need to do the best race I can. With experience, you learn how to move forward. Of course, this weekend has been a bit off with everything, but tomorrow I think we can do a good race."
keyPointsZh: 安东内利在Q1第一弯左侧弯撞上内侧护墙，导致悬挂损坏，被迫停下梅赛德斯W17赛车。
他的首个飞驰圈本已足以晋级Q2，但无法继续参赛；队友拉塞尔以0.8秒优势夺得杆位。
安东内利因液压问题缺席了周四大部分练习，他承认自己“没有百分之百在状态”，并称巴库想复制蒙扎的翻盘会更难。
keyPointsEn: Antonelli tagged the inside wall at the Turn 1 left-hander in Q1, causing terminal suspension damage that forced him to park his Mercedes W17.
His first flying lap had already been good enough for Q2, but he could not take part; teammate George Russell took pole by eight tenths.
Antonelli missed a large chunk of Thursday practice due to a hydraulic issue, admitted he "wasn't 100 percent there", and said a Monza-style comeback would be harder in Baku.

items.originalTitle: Jamie Chadwick points to 'Kimi Antonelli of old' after Baku qualifying mistake
items.summaryEn: Sky Sports F1 pundit Jamie Chadwick believes Kimi Antonelli's Q1 crash in Azerbaijan Grand Prix qualifying was a return to old habits, calling it an unnecessary risk given Mercedes' pace. Antonelli will start 16th, but 1997 F1 champion Jacques Villeneuve still backs him to make his way back through the field.
detailZh: 查德威克：安东内利巴库排位失误是旧习复发
杰米·查德威克认为，基米·安东内利在巴库Q1不必要的撞车是旧习复发
天空体育F1评论员杰米·查德威克声称，基米·安东内利在阿塞拜疆大奖赛排位赛中的撞车是旧习复发，并称他在Q1的撞车是鉴于梅赛德斯的速度优势而冒的不必要风险。
安东内利目前在车手积分榜上领先队友乔治·拉塞尔81分，他在巴库城市赛道这条不容犯错的街道赛上擦墙，提前结束了排位赛。
赛车左前部受损意味着他的排位赛就此结束，而他的队友兼最接近的冠军竞争对手则夺得了杆位。
“我说这是反常的。我们经常看到基米开车的方式是只有一个挡位。就是全力推进。就是倾其所有，”查德威克在天空体育转播中解释道。
“去年我们看到这带来了失误和撞车。今年我们还没有真正从他身上看到这种情况。所以感觉有点像过去的基米，就是那种只有一个挡位，而他其实并不需要这么做。
“话虽如此，我认为在这样的赛道上很容易犯这样的错误，我们知道这一点。但你驾驶的是一辆在这条赛道上明显独一档的梅赛德斯，Q1的第一圈，你不需要冒那么大的风险。
“只是他在1号弯明显拥有的抓地力让他措手不及。进入排位赛时，赛车总是比他在三练时更活跃一些，这让他措手不及。他会付出代价，但我认为他明天仍然能够追回来。”
安东内利将从第16位发车参加阿塞拜疆大奖赛。尽管起步位置不利，1997年F1世界冠军雅克·维伦纽夫仍支持这位意大利车手在赛道上追回位置。
“这不是一英寸的事，而是差了很多。一个不可思议的失误，而且他是在队友独一档的周末犯下的，”这位加拿大人对天空体育F1表示。
“所以，这个时机不太好，但根据现行规则，它们有利于在赛道上追回位置。”
detailEn: Jamie Chadwick points to 'Kimi Antonelli of old' after Baku qualifying mistake
Jamie Chadwick believes Kimi Antonelli reverted to old habits with an unnecessary Q1 crash in Baku

Sky Sports Formula 1 pundit Jamie Chadwick has claimed that Kimi Antonelli's crash during qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix was a return to old habits, branding his Q1 shunt an unnecessary risk given Mercedes' pace.

Antonelli, who currently leads the drivers' championship by 81 points over his team-mate George Russell, prematurely ended his qualifying session after clipping the wall on the unforgiving streets of the Baku City Circuit.
The damage sustained to the front-left of the car meant his qualifying was over as his team-mate and closest championship rival went on to secure pole position.
"I say it's uncharacteristic. The way we see Kimi drive a lot of the time is that there's one gear. It's all in. It's all everything," Chadwick explained during the Sky Sports broadcast.

"Last year we saw that come with mistakes and crashes. This year we have not really seen that from him. So it has felt a bit like Kimi of old in a way and it was like that one gear and he just didn't really need to do it.

"That said, I think it is easy to make mistakes like that, we know that at a track like this. But you are in a Mercedes that was clearly in a league of its own at this track, first lap of Q1, you didn't need to take that much risk.

"It just caught him out, the grip that he clearly had at Turn 1. You go into qualifying, and the car is always a bit more alive I guess than it would have been for him in FP3, and it has caught him out. He will pay the price, but I think he can still come through tomorrow."

Antonelli will start the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 16th on the grid. Despite the starting position, 1997 F1 champion Jacques Villeneuve backed the Italian driver to make his way back through the field.
"It's not an inch, it's a lot. An incredible mistake and he does it on a weekend where his team-mate is in a league of his own," the Canadian told Sky Sports F1.
"So, not the best of times for that, but with the current rules they facilitate getting back through the field."
keyPointsZh: 安东内利在车手积分榜上领先队友乔治·拉塞尔81分。
安东内利在巴库街道赛擦墙导致左前部受损，排位赛提前结束，拉塞尔夺得杆位。
维伦纽夫称这是“一个不可思议的失误”，但认为现行规则有利于他追回位置。
keyPointsEn: Antonelli leads the drivers' championship by 81 points over his team-mate George Russell.
Antonelli clipped the wall on the Baku street circuit, damaging the front-left of his car and ending his qualifying early, while Russell secured pole position.
Villeneuve called it 'an incredible mistake' but believes current rules facilitate his recovery through the field.
